cases.title: A connected toolkit for a remodeling business
cases.sum: A public website, an office workspace, a job tracker for crews and a set of video ads, in place of a spreadsheet and a crowded inbox.

• A public website with service pages and 57 plain-spoken local remodeling guides
  • An office workspace for inbox review, estimates, payments and job details
  • A mobile layout designed for crews in the field, tracking hours, costs and what each job really earns
  • Short video ads in six styles, queued on a weekly posting schedule

• Larger text and five clear groups make the office workspace easy for the owner to use every day
  • Customer data stays on the owner’s computer
  • The AI drafts and organizes; nothing reaches the books or a customer until the owner approves it
  • Careful checks against representative business data before delivery

about.label: Meet Myles
body: I’m Myles Parslow. I started MLP Consulting to build the websites and behind-the-scenes systems that owner-run businesses rarely have time to set up for themselves.

I studied philosophy at USC, and I build things. A remodeling company’s office system that reads the inbox, tracks job costs and shows what each job really earned. A real estate website with eight AI tools for its agents. A lead map drawn from more than 11,000 city building permits. The seventeen sites in the work section above.

My background is in law-firm conflicts and risk, where a missed detail has consequences and nothing goes out unchecked. I run projects the same way: the scope is written down, you approve what customers see, and the handoff is documented. I’m based in Irvine.
about.quote: “The money is usually leaking somewhere else, like quotes nobody followed up on or invoices that sat for two months before anyone asked.”

how.lead: How a project runs, what stays in your control, and answers to the questions owners ask before we talk.
steps: Pick the first thing to fix
We walk through how inquiries, quotes and payments move through your business, and pick the fix that pays off soonest.
You get a written proposal: what gets built, the price, the timeline and any software costs. Nothing starts until you say yes.
I build it, we run it on real examples until it’s right, and I show your team how to use it. Support continues after launch.
how.principles_h2: Built for your business. Kept in your control.
principles: You approve the messages and rules before launch. Routine work follows those rules, and decisions that need your judgment come back to you.
Your domain, business accounts, and customer data stay yours. You receive the access and documentation needed to manage the work.
You work with me directly, from the first conversation through delivery and support. Call or email and I’m the one who answers.
how.faq_h2: Good to know before we talk.
faq: Start with the free assessment. I’ll review your public website and online presence, then recommend three practical improvements. We can use a short conversation to identify the best fit for your team and budget.
Can you work with the software I already use?
Yes. The starting point is your current setup. I look for ways to improve and connect what you have, and recommend changes when they make the work simpler.
Do I need to know anything about AI?
You bring your knowledge of the business. I handle the technical setup and explain how the tools fit into the work your team already does.

Website care starts at $200 per month, with hosting, backups, security updates, and agreed content changes. Support for connected workflows is scoped around the systems involved and the level of service you need.
What happens after I contact you?
I’ll review what you’ve shared and recommend a useful next step. When there’s a project to pursue, you’ll receive a clear scope and price before work starts.

meta.og_description: Six practical workflows MLP Consulting sets up for owner-run businesses: inquiry follow-up, quote follow-up, payment reminders, review requests, missed-call follow-up and a weekly owner summary.

workflows.h1: Useful workflows for a busy business.
workflows.lead: Six moves that take routine follow-up off your plate. Each is set up on the tools you already use, in your wording.

cards.when: A form, call or message arrives
cards.title: New inquiry follow-up
cards.text: A prompt acknowledgment goes out in your words, asks a couple of useful questions, and offers a time to talk. You are alerted right away if it looks like a larger job.
cards.rule_html: Control: You approve the first reply, once, before launch.

cards.title: Quote follow-up
cards.text: Friendly check-ins on day 2, 5 and 10, plus a list of who has gone quiet. A customer’s reply pauses that quote’s sequence and alerts you.
cards.rule_html: Control: You approve each message until you trust the wording.

cards.when: An invoice passes its due date
cards.title: Payment reminders
cards.text: A polite reminder, then a firmer one, each with a way to pay. You hear about it at two weeks, and the sequence stops once payment is received.
cards.rule_html: Control: You approve the tone and decide on any call.

cards.when: A job or visit is finished
cards.title: Review requests
cards.text: Make it easy for customers to share honest feedback after a completed job or visit, with a consistent request process and a clear route for your team to respond.
cards.rule_html: Control: You approve who gets asked and the wording.

cards.title: Missed-call follow-up
cards.text: A text within a minute asking what’s going on and offering a callback time, logged as a lead so no call is lost. A reply pauses the text and alerts the right person.
cards.rule_html: Control: You approve the wording and the hours it runs.

cards.title: Weekly owner summary
cards.text: One short message: new inquiries, quotes waiting, money overdue, and the one thing to do first. It goes only to you.
cards.rule_html: Control: Nothing to approve; it never contacts a customer.

workflows.note_h2: Clear approvals and a pause button
workflows.note: Before anything goes live, we write down what each workflow may do on its own, what waits for you, and what it never does. Every message and approval is logged, and you can pause everything at once. Where a customer replies, the relevant follow-up sequence pauses and the right person is alerted.

meta.description: How MLP Consulting handles information submitted through this website.
meta.og_description: How MLP Consulting handles information submitted through this website.

privacy.lead: A plain description of what happens to information you share on this site.
sections: When you use the contact form, you share your name, business name, email, and optionally your website, a note about what you would like to improve, and who referred you. We use it to review your business and reply to you.

Form submissions are delivered to myles@mlpconsults.com through Web3Forms, and a copy is stored in MLP Consulting’s customer relationship tools (HubSpot) and a database (Supabase) so requests can be tracked. We do not sell your information.
The “Book a free 30-minute call” link opens a scheduling page hosted by Cal.com. Information you enter there is handled under Cal.com’s own policies.

This site loads HubSpot’s tracking script, which sets a cookie so form submissions can be matched to visits. Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts. The site is hosted on Cloudflare, which keeps standard server logs.
To ask what we hold about you, or to have it removed, email myles@mlpconsults.com.
